paper.title: High H2 Uptake by Alkali-Doped Carbon Nanotubes Under Ambient Pressure and Moderate Temperatures

defaults.verified_by: Agent B (sonnet, independent re-derivation of Table 1 + Figs 1A/1B + schema): 5 rows. The four discredited uptakes (Li-CNT 20.0, Li-graphite 14.0, K-CNT 14.0, K-graphite 5.0 wt%) and the undoped-CNT 0.4 wt% baseline all confirmed against Table 1, with the two 14.0s correctly separated and the energy column (wt% x 33.3 kWh/kg) cross-checking. This is the CONTROVERSY paper (Chen 1999 Science): Yang 2000 (Carbon 38:623) showed the TGA weight gain was largely moisture, dry H2 ~2 wt%, so the four doped rows are retained at Tier D with the discrepancy per S13.6 (HYC-0011 precedent). measurement_method=gravimetric_microbalance (TGA); measurement_mode=temperature_cycle with reference_temperature_k = complete-desorption T (Li 823 K, K 773 K); the 653 K Li absorption exceeds temperature_k's 500 K cap so temperature_unstated=True (653 K in source_location). Agent C accepted Agent B's disputes: doped CNT material_class doped_carbon->MWCNT (a doped nanotube keeps its structural class + dopant_element, HYC-0025/0037 precedent; also correctly fires the pre-2005-raw-CNT warning the earlier call lost); doped graphite doped_carbon->other (no graphite class); pressure 1 atm 1.01->1.01325 bar (HYC-0029 convention). Agent C added the undoped-CNT 0.4 wt% baseline row per Agent B (S3.2/S7.4 null result), at Tier C (scorer; a baseline, not a discredited claim) rather than the hand D. The 14.5 wt% 673 K ramp transient was declined as a separate row (explicitly non-equilibrium, same sample) and kept in notes. Comparison rows (FeTi-H, NiMg-H, cryoadsorption, isooctane) and the Vi density column excluded. Introduces one new warning type, 'Uptake above 10 wt%' (3 rows).

notes.disc: DISCREDITED boom-bust claim (controversy set S6.7). Yang 2000 (Carbon 38:623) showed the TGA weight gain was largely moisture/H2O in the purge gas; dry H2 gave ~2 wt% (~7-10x lower). Retained at Tier D with the discrepancy per S13.6 (HYC-0011 precedent). Values are the paper's own Table 1 / text figures.
notes.method: TGA thermobalance under flowing purified H2 (>99.99%), confirmed by TPD; in-situ FTIR shows dissociative hydrogenation (C-H, Li-H, Li2C2) -- chemisorption. measurement_method=gravimetric_microbalance. No sample mass / blank / buoyancy / calibration / uncertainty reported (only >99.99% gas purity).
notes.cycle: weight gain over a thermal ramp/hold in flowing H2 -> measurement_mode=temperature_cycle (HYC-0029): absorption T = temperature_k, complete-desorption T = reference_temperature_k. Li: absorb 653 K / desorb 823 K; 653 K exceeds the 500 K temperature_k cap, so temperature_unstated=True (653 K stated in source_location). Li-CNT also reached 14.5 wt% at 673 K on the 5 K/min ramp (NON-equilibrium; not recorded as a row). K: absorb 298 K / desorb 773 K. ambient pressure 1 atm = 1.01325 bar.
notes.class: doped nanotube keeps its structural class -> MWCNT + dopant_element (HYC-0025/0037); doped graphite -> other (no graphite class) + dopant_element. base CNT from CH4 CVD (>90% MWCNT, 25-35 nm, interplanar 0.347 nm, SSA 130); base graphite Merck 50 um, SSA 8.6. Li/C or K/C ~1/15 (atomic ratio) by XPS. bet_surface_area is the UNDOPED host SSA; surface_area_method=unspecified.
notes.base: undoped CNT baseline 0.4 wt% (Table 1 'CNT' row, attrib. ref 9; 'or no H2 absorption' so possibly <=0.4) over a 298-773 K scan -> no single T (temperature_unstated), Tier C (a baseline, not a discredited claim). Undoped graphite 'no absorption' (no number) -> note only.
notes.excl: Table 1 comparison rows (FeTi-H, NiMg-H, cryoadsorption, isooctane) and intro Dillon/Chambers/Ye values excluded (non-carbon / not this work). Vi density column not recorded (180/12.6/280 g/L internally inconsistent, S3.7).
